title: The Strange Unsolved Murder of Ken McElroy
summary: Josh and Chuck (with Olivia doing research) examine the 1980 killing of Ken Rex McElroy in Skidmore, Missouri, a cattle thief and serial sexual predator who avoided conviction in more than twenty charges through lawyer Gene McFadden and witness intimidation. After he shot grocer Bo Bowen Camp and was released on bond, a crowd of townspeople followed him to the DNG Tavern and shot him dead in his truck; no one was ever charged. The episode covers the Richard Stratton arrest, the 1980 shooting, the town's silence, the FBI closing its investigation in 1982, and the later fates of the people involved. Includes a short ad break and a listener mail segment about the Grand Canyon river speed record episode. Includes a trigger warning for child sexual abuse content.

segments.title: Ken McElroy's background and cattle theft
segments.summary: McElroy's childhood in a large poor family, his early crime, a head injury from a construction accident, his side businesses including hunting dogs and antiques, and the county's high cattle theft rate that he drove. His imposing size and cash-heavy lifestyle are described.

segments.title: Lawyer Gene McFadden and witness intimidation
segments.summary: McFadden, a Kansas City lawyer, took McElroy as a cash client. Delays and intimidation of witnesses and jurors kept McElroy from conviction, earning him the nickname Teflon-coated criminal.

segments.title: Shooting of Romayne Henry and the town's intimidation
segments.summary: McElroy shot Romayne Henry in the stomach over pheasant hunting on his land and got off through alibi witnesses. He also threatened a highway patrolman's family and held Margaret, a cop's wife, at gunpoint. Judges and the county magistrate were intimidated.

segments.title: Sexual abuse and serial marriages
segments.summary: The hosts describe McElroy's sexual abuse of underage girls, serial marriages used to prevent wives from testifying, his marriage to Trina McLeod at age fifteen, and his violent response to her parents.

segments.title: Foster care attempt and final marriage
segments.summary: After Trina reported the abuse to a doctor, she was placed with a foster family, which McElroy stalked. She later returned to him, and they married with her parents' consent under threat, with McFadden as witness.

segments.title: Shooting of Bo Bowen Camp and arrest
segments.summary: McElroy's stealing trouble with the Bowen Camp grocery, then he shot grocer Bo Bowen Camp in the neck in July 1980. Highway patrolman Richard Stratton anticipated his escape route and arrested him in Fillmore, Missouri.

segments.title: Self-defense defense and threats against the town
segments.summary: McFadden moved the trial to Harrison County and planned a self-defense claim. McElroy kept intimidating the Bowen Camps and the local minister Tim Warren, whose wife was threatened.

segments.title: Town marshal and the sheriff's failure to act
segments.summary: Town marshal David Dunbar quit after McElroy held him at gunpoint. The sheriff was reportedly unresponsive to calls. The trial took nearly a year to start, and prosecutor David Baird, newly appointed, won a second-degree assault conviction and two years' sentence.

segments.title: Bond release and threats at the tavern
segments.summary: McElroy was released on forty thousand dollars bond. He then threatened to finish off Bo Bowen Camp at the DNG Tavern, prompting Pete Ward and his sons to seek a bond revocation hearing.

segments.title: Town meeting at the American Legion and the tavern confrontation
segments.summary: Around a hundred adults gathered at the American Legion Hall. The bond hearing was delayed to July twentieth. Sheriff Danny Estes offered no help, and about fifty to sixty people went to the DNG Tavern where McElroy defiantly left.

segments.title: Killing of Ken McElroy outside the DNG Tavern
segments.summary: A crowd surrounded McElroy's Silverado in the DNG Tavern parking lot. He was shot in the head and neck by two different calibers of bullets, with his wife Trina beside him. The truck crashed and the crowd dispersed.

segments.title: Investigation, silence and conflicting accounts
segments.summary: No witness would cooperate and no one was charged. One witness named Dell Clement and another man; Trina later identified Dell Clement as shooter. Accounts about the gun and the head disposal are unverified, and a Vietnam veteran said he would have done more.

segments.title: Trina's fear, FBI closure and mob justice debate
segments.summary: Newspaper accounts recorded Trina's fear; townspeople disagreed. The FBI closed its investigation on September 2, 1982, and the hosts discuss whether mob justice was justified.

segments.title: Aftermath for Clement, Trina, McFadden and Stratton
segments.summary: Dell Clement died in 2009 without comment. Trina's 1985 wrongful death suit settled for $17,600. She remarried and died in 2012. McFadden remained proud of his work, and Richard Stratton believed law enforcement had failed the town.

segments.title: Listener mail on Kenton Grua and the Grand Canyon speed record
segments.summary: Listener Noah explains the eleven pm start time for the Kenton Grua Grand Canyon river speed record run as a way to hit the rapids in daylight.
